avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, control of emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own means: money from parks funds, machinery rental, blue-collar crews. Variances also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its reserved fund for park purposes to buy trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an addition at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the chalet in parc Pratt and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council rents land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain, for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees there for planting.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report no later than December 31, 2026, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the nursery in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs rented vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives from streets, sidewalks and bike paths. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, sidewalk cleaning in four private snow removal sectors was awarded to a company for $271,979.11, taxes included [CA26 27 0034].

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie awarded companies contracts for snow removal, spreading of abrasives and maintenance of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six public squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough also extended the Quartier des Spectacles snow removal contract by one year, from April 2, 2026, to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord approved an additional expense of $106,150.97, taxes included, for the rental of an extra grader [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard took $200,000 from its surpluses for staff pay and the purchase of abrasives, and Verdun offered to have city council supply the staff for the snow disposal site itself.

The City extended turnkey snow removal contracts by twelve months in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, as well as towing contracts and equipment rentals with operators in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Boroughs did the same for vehicle and loader-tractor rentals.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal equipment rental services in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie start on November 1, 2026, and the extension runs until March 31, 2027.
The extended towing contracts start on November 15, 2026.
Snow removal in the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers two seasons, from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2028.
The turnkey contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030; the one for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its drinking water and sewer networks, in several boroughs and on main pipes. It is also continuing the wastewater disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and paying for the day-to-day operation of this plant. Boroughs are taking charge of replacing lead water service connections, including the portion located on private land.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining, without digging trenches, and to redo the roadway in various streets in many boroughs. These contracts include the replacement of lead water service connections on both the public side and the private side.

etapes.titre: Lead water service connections on private land
etapes.texte: Boroughs are offering city council the option to take charge of replacing lead service connections located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the property owners concerned [CA26 22 0034].

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild water pipes and infrastructure along rue Guy and on rue De Champlain, and is adding funds to the contracts for rue Saint-Antoine Ouest and rue de la Cathédrale. On rue De Champlain, the project replaces a 1,200 mm pipe installed in 1927 [CG26 0332].

The City is renewing or awarding contracts to operate the wastewater treatment plant: process control system, chemical products, residue landfilling, housekeeping, upgrading of sludge incinerators, and mechanical work. The mechanical work is aimed in particular at reconditioning screens damaged during heavy rainfalls [CG26 0543].

aSurveiller.texte: Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026, then incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Adoption expected on October 19, 2026, of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
Rehabilitation work on the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord to be completed by December 18, 2026, at the latest.
Completion of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Rue Guy project expected to run until December 2027; the ozone plant is expected to come into service in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back park and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on several projects at Frédéric-Back park and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. It is launching construction of a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, replacing electrical equipment at the site, renewing park maintenance, and redeveloping rue De Louvain near the park. It is also asking the Quebec government for funding for a cycling and pedestrian link.

etapes.texte: The City is requesting financial assistance from the Quebec ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The file describes a 900-metre trail crossing the park, including a footbridge of about 150 metres, and funding of up to $2,000,000 [CG26 0121].

The City approves construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform, then hands the project to the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough. The borough then awards a contract of $499,865.92, taxes included, to supply and install two greenhouses, with $74,979.88 in contingencies [CA26 14 0163].

The City awards a contract of $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, with $163,754.01 in contingencies. The work involves a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator, and a controller to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223].

The borough awards a contract of up to $8,199,514.82, taxes included, to redevelop rue De Louvain between Frédéric-Back park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a total authorized expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, the bike path, and plantings [CA26 14 0076].

The City entrusts two companies with general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028. It also extends by six months the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ, and the soccer stadium, for $193,215.49 more, taxes included [CG26 0521].

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the complex, for $296,349.21 more, taxes included; the compost is used in part to landscape the park [CG26 0320]. In October, the borough authorizes submitting a funding request to the Véloce III program for the bike lane and sidewalks on rue De Louvain Est.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is submitting its application, closes on November 26, 2026.
Greenhouse installation work is expected to finish in December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The extended snow removal contract covers November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs by unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that must be cleaned by hand, additional mortar, sod, and a deteriorated culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. Filing the application involves no expense; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two sectors added as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are added to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité of the agglomeration, with conservation plans. The 2025 report filed shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, or 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

etapes.titre: Reconstruction of the chemin Senneville culvert
etapes.texte: A contract for $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to reconstruct the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; the total expense reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow removal, cleaning and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the snow removal of service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors ($178,330.82, taxes included), and 9232-3914 Québec inc. the cleaning of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other dying trees in the park, for a total expense of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Cleaning of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and dying trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan filed in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is putting in place a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026, and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for the 2025-2026 winter.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and fitting-out of the Bain St-Denis
etapes.texte: Council adopts a framework to receive private donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fitting-out work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal proceedings
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract worth $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to support people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes over the litigation on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026, ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and projects for social, affordable or student housing, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: This year, the City approves the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the OMHM, transfers or buys land intended for social housing, and pays grants to organizations building affordable housing. It also amends the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units [CM26 0114]. City council and the urban agglomeration council approve the 2026 budget of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households [CG26 0024].

The City accepts from the Government of Canada half the rights to a 3,658.8 square metre lot on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost [CG26 0042]. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a 789.6 square metre lot at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, where the cooperative must build 26 housing units [CG26 0062].

The City adds $877,312 to its support for Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve [CG26 0171]. It grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project [CG26 0178].

etapes.titre: Land purchase and right of first refusal
etapes.texte: The City buys, for $9,293,113, plus taxes, a vacant 1,535.1 square metre lot near rue Chatham and rue William, in the Sud-Ouest, for social housing purposes [CG26 0286]. It withdraws the right of first refusal for social housing on lots in Ville-Marie and the Sud-Ouest that had been targeted since 2020 [CG26 0292].

The City pays $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel for 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus [CG26 0372] and $13,151,528 to Immobilier collectif – Point commun for 395 housing units in Pointe-Saint-Charles [CG26 0559]. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build 72 housing units on 2e Avenue [CE26 1028], and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a policy to reimburse 50% of permit fees for eligible projects [CA26 170209].

aSurveiller.texte: Occupancy of the 350 housing units at Technopôle Angus by no later than April 30, 2027.
Delivery of the SHDM's 72-unit building on 2e Avenue in May 2028.
Occupancy of the 395-unit building in Pointe-Saint-Charles in February 2030.
Integration of the fee exemption into the 2027 local fee by-law in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council extended the lease of a 2,787 square metre lot to the Société de transport de Montréal, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, for a total rent of $49,293. It also extended the lease of a neighbouring 836 square metre lot to an app-based parking company, for $45,049 before taxes.

City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités", because the first residential project is under construction and addresses need to be assigned. The name came from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Contract for the street and soils
etapes.texte: The City awarded Charex inc. the construction of a 610-metre street with sewer, water supply, lighting and underground electrical network, for $10,311,940.25 including taxes, and a total expenditure of $15,366,336. The contract includes the remediation of the soil at the former gas station, for which the City is adding $2,007,312.15 net through the environmental liability reserve.

The borough adopted a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a group of buildings, with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It then launched a draft by-law allowing, on part of the municipal lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, a height limit of 73 metres and a floor area ratio of 6.

etapes.titre: Redevelopment of rue de Louvain Est
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes and a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. In October, it authorized the filing of a financial assistance request to the ministère des Transports for the bike lane and sidewalks on this section.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027; the Ville en vert vegetable garden is loaned out until December 31, 2027.
Îlot 84 could occupy the Esplanade lot from April 1 to October 31, 2027.
Work on rue de Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks and curbs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
Four other public spaces in the eco-district remain to be named before the development is completed, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its ecocentre-related contracts, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the 2025 report on the agglomeration's residual materials management.

etapes.texte: The City extends twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanize food waste from the east of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, pending the start-up of the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre.

etapes.titre: Purchase of bins and loan of sorting equipment
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations at neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The agglomeration extends the collection contracts for garbage from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from the ecocentres, entrusts two firms with studies on buildings located on former waste disposal sites, and extends the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program to lend dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until no later than December 31, 2026.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The contract for the dumping authorization management software covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water supply for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It has obtained an extra delay from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for the water supply system and public domain, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline extended to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a delay until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension involves no financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of assets and public funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and water supply, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build water supply trunk mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and recreation centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and facilities in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the MultiCaf community cafeteria and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transitional nursery. Each lease provides for a token rent, and the organizations pay for development, upkeep and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The federal grant of $128.3M is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031; the funds from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the transfer deed to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora, and April 30, 2028 for the transitional nursery.

parcs.description: Development and upgrading of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.

etapes.titre: Plans and studies before the work
etapes.texte: The City is giving the winning team of an architecture competition the job of designing the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and redeveloping the parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil and environmental studies of the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, having a culvert rebuilt at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche, and awarding contracts for snow clearing and the cutting down of ash trees and dying trees. It is adding the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the registry of protected natural environments and submitting the candidacy of Cap-Saint-Jacques for Urban Night Sky Place designation.

The City and the boroughs are adding amounts or shifting budgets for work already underway: oversight of the parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parcs des Hirondelles and du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray, plans for the parc Percy-Walters, and museum display design for the parc des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne in Lachine.

City council is removing a 810.2 m² stretch of street from the public domain to add it to the parc Campbell Ouest, in Le Sud-Ouest. Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is requesting the same for a 75.2 m² strip of laneway that crosses the parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: City council must vote on October 19, 2026, on removing the laneway strip from the parc Le Prévost, after it goes through the executive committee on October 7, 2026.
For the artwork at the parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026, and installation in 2028.
The snow clearing contract for the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers the period from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2028.
Final acceptance of the work at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois is expected in June 2027, after the warranty year.
For the Cap-Saint-Jacques candidacy: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, and site compliance work in April 2032.
Work on the parc J.O.R.-Leduc, in LaSalle, is expected to finish in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and by-laws for commercial activities.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and regulating temporary pedestrian streets on commercial thoroughfares, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid out $2,694,500 to the boroughs as part of the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial thoroughfares [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted by-laws that close streets, authorize terraces, sales, and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a lot, and an official name.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by order [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee distributes $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the commercial development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their thoroughfares to cars and set rules for terraces, sales, and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) to local park [CM26 0888] and names "place Chez-Marguerite" the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between rue Saint-Denis and rue Resther on September 30, 2026, and between rue Saint-Laurent and rue Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
The boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The by-law on sound ambiance for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract for avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministère
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, that is until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting six additional months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

After the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is reviewing its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing the heights, uses and building footprint ratio in the sector bordered by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing the heights allowed on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent's public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the extension granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, the date set by the minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and to hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's Police Department (SPVM): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: City council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to purchase and replace specialized public safety equipment for the SPVM between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City awards 9415-1966 Québec inc. the contract for meals for persons detained by the SPVM and extends by one year the computer-aided dispatch system software maintenance contract with Peraton International. It leases 50 parking spaces from the Société de la Place des arts, extends the lease of the training centre in Anjou and that of neighbourhood station 15 in Verdun, and accepts $8,000 from Ottawa for a sexual assault awareness campaign.

The City signs an agreement with Agence Gravel for 9 mm practice ammunition for firearms training, extends the SPVM's courier contract by one year, and renews the lease for neighbourhood station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings, and lends a detective sergeant to the Sûreté du Québec team working on the export of stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: October 23, 2026: "Fèves au lard" day organized by the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood station 46, for which the borough of Anjou purchased 62 tickets.
February 1, 2027: start of the 10-year lease for the metro unit's space at neighbourhood station 50, located at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.
March 1, 2027: deadline for delivery of the harbour patrol boat and its trailer.
March 31, 2027: end of the period covered by the grants from the ACCES Tabac, ACCES Alcool, ACCES Cannabis, and ACCEF committees.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and loan by-laws of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then sells, leases or lends it land to expand metro stations and facilities. It also signs agreements to carry out municipal work at the same time as the blue line extension work, and oversees metro and REM construction sites. Borough councils also adopt motions on network development.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council approves the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410, and its 2026-2035 capital works program [CG26 0022]. The City also enters into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, for a maximum of $41,944,604.63 including taxes, plus contingencies [CG26 0064].

etapes.titre: Land sold, leased and lent to the STM
etapes.texte: The City sells the STM a 364.3 m² plot of land near the Place-Saint-Henri station for $495,150 plus taxes [CG26 0348], land in Verdun for the Rielle ventilation station [CG26 0349], and commits to selling a portion of rue Jean-Brillant for a rectifier station [CG26 0375]. It also leases a parking lot to the STM in Ahuntsic-Cartierville [CM26 0078], lends it a small building on rue Stinson for its drivers [CE26 1303], and signs an access agreement for a plot of land on boulevard Décarie [CA26 170103].

etapes.titre: Work entrusted to the STM and bus stops
etapes.texte: The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes spending of $3,808,451.29 including taxes [CG26 0175]. It also signs an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion at parc Irma-LeVasseur, backing onto a metro ventilation station in Outremont [CM26 0198], while Ahuntsic-Cartierville establishes and removes bus waiting areas as part of the network redesign [CA26 09 0020].

The urban agglomeration council approves several STM loans: metro infrastructure rehabilitation, surface building rehabilitation, preferential measures for buses, cybersecurity, extending the service life of MR-73 cars, and analysis of their replacement. The 2026-2035 Capital Works Program is amended each time.

The City retains Artelia Canada and Stantec Experts-conseils for the redevelopment of the blue line corridor, from Saint-Michel to Anjou, for an estimated amount of $19,070,092.68 including taxes [CG26 0564]. The city council asks Québec to study preserving the tunnel boring machine from the blue line extension [CM26 0920]; Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring projects in the East and in the Grand Sud-Ouest, Anjou asks for the study of a reserved lane on rue Beaubien to be stopped, and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building bus stop sidewalks.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the parking lot south of rue de Louvain begins on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Rehabilitation and expansion work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for at most two weeks during the summer 2027 vacation period; bridge-tunnel work is expected to continue until March 2028.
The opening of the five stations of the blue line extension is expected in 2031; integrated municipal work is planned for 2028-2029.
Professional services agreements for the blue line corridor run from October 2026 to October 2032.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the BIXI bike-share.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI bike-share, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new bike-related projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an order that makes official the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rues des Carrières and de Bellechasse, and requires drivers to make mandatory maneuvers up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives, spread notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for the sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved that Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carry out roadway and bike lane work, including repairs to the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville hired Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of the narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then hired Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17 to supply the steel pavers that serve as the base for the stations.

Outremont filed a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and the Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

City council authorized the filing of four funding requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to file complete funding requests with the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike lane on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
